newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil output seen down in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil output seen down in Nov.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in November is estimated to have fallen by up to 19 percent against October, plantation houses said on Thursday.
Output in October was 883,579 tonnes, official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) data showed.
"The fall was expected. This is the seasonal downtrend in output. November, December, January and February are always the low crop months," an official at a plantation firm said.
"The fall in East Malaysian states particularly Sabah would be bad because of the wet weather conditions," he said.

Malaysian private forecaster, Ivan Wong, who is expected to release his final November crop estimates on Friday, said in his previous report that output in November would fall by 14 percent to 764,000 tonnes.
PORLA will release its November crop data on December 16.
Traders had projected end-November stocks at 965,000 tonnes against 953,241 tonnes at end-October.
Exports in November were estimated at 655,000 tonnes against 727,629 tonnes in October.
